Critical flaw in Examplar Edge Gateway lets attackers bypass OIDC checks

By Jane Fixture, 23 September 2026

Examplar Networks has released fixes for a critical authentication bypass in its Edge Gateway product, tracked as CVE-2026-41234 and rated 9.8 on the CVSS v3.1 scale. The flaw affects Edge Gateway versions 5.2.0 through 5.2.7 and allows an unauthenticated attacker to present a crafted ID token that the gateway accepts without verifying its signature.

The issue was reported by researcher Priya Raman of Northwind Security, who said the gateway “trusted the alg header supplied by the client” when validating tokens issued by an external identity provider. Examplar said version 5.2.8, published on 22 September, corrects the validation logic.

According to the advisory, customers who cannot upgrade immediately should set the strict_jwks option to true, which forces the gateway to reject tokens whose algorithm does not match the key type registered for the issuer. The company said it had seen no evidence of exploitation at the time of publication.

Northwind Security said it found 1,200 internet-facing Edge Gateway instances running an affected version during a scan on 20 September. Raman said organisations using the gateway in front of payment APIs should treat the upgrade as urgent.

The disclosure follows a similar token validation issue in another vendor's ingress controller earlier this year, which prompted renewed attention to RFC 8725, the JSON Web Token Best Current Practices document.
